issues.label: Appellate jurisdiction and timeliness
issues.why: The court must confirm a final appealable order and that any appeal was timely and properly perfected.

issues.label: Proper consolidation of cases
issues.why: The court must ensure joinder/consolidation complied with Crim.R. 13/8 and did not prejudice Hampton.

issues.label: Effect of guilty pleas
issues.why: The court must determine which claims were waived by the guilty pleas and which survive (e.g., sentencing legality, jurisdiction).

issues.label: Voluntariness of pleas
issues.why: If implicated, the court must confirm Crim.R. 11 compliance and that pleas were knowing, intelligent, and voluntary.

issues.label: Factual basis for pleas
issues.why: The court should consider whether the record supports the elements of the offenses pled, especially for complex offenses.

issues.label: Sentencing statutory ranges
issues.why: Each prison term must fall within the applicable statutory range for the degree of offense.

issues.label: Correct offense levels
issues.why: The court must verify each offense’s felony degree/misdemeanor level and corresponding sentencing range.

issues.label: Failure-to-comply level
issues.why: The court must confirm the specific R.C. 2921.331 penalty tier pled and whether the imposed term matches it.

issues.label: Dangerous ordnance offense validity
issues.why: The court must ensure the dangerous ordnance charge and its elements were properly charged/pled and sentenced under the correct statute.

issues.label: Receiving stolen property grading
issues.why: The court must confirm the property value/type or vehicle status supports the felony degree used at sentencing.

issues.label: Vehicular assault grading
issues.why: The court must verify whether the vehicular assault counts are F3/F4 and whether the 12-month terms were lawful.

issues.label: Aggravated vehicular homicide grading
issues.why: The court must confirm the felony level and mandatory/prison-eligibility provisions for R.C. 2903.06(A)(2)(a).

issues.label: Involuntary manslaughter grading
issues.why: The court must ensure the underlying felony and plea correspond to the correct degree and range.

issues.label: Failure to stop after accident grading
issues.why: The court must confirm the count pled (e.g., injury/death) matches the penalty level and 36-month term.

issues.label: Allied offenses merger analysis
issues.why: The court must determine whether any convictions should merge under R.C. 2941.25 (e.g., homicide/manslaughter/vehicular assault/RSP/FTSAA).

issues.label: Merger procedure and election
issues.why: If offenses merge, the court must ensure the State made an election and the court entered a single conviction/sentence.

issues.label: Multiple victims considerations
issues.why: The court must assess whether separate harms/victims permit separate convictions and consecutive terms despite overlap.

issues.label: Firearm specification legality
issues.why: The court must ensure the firearm specification(s) pled are authorized for the underlying offense(s) and properly imposed.

issues.label: Spec mandatory consecutive nature
issues.why: Firearm-spec prison time must be imposed and served consecutively as required by statute.

issues.label: Spec stacking limits
issues.why: The court must apply statutory limits on imposing multiple firearm specs in the same case/transaction, if applicable.

issues.label: Six-year spec applicability
issues.why: The court must confirm the factual/legal basis for a six-year spec (e.g., automatic firearm, dangerous ordnance, or similar qualifier).

issues.label: Nine-month term lawfulness
issues.why: The court must ensure the 9-month term imposed is authorized for the specific offense degree (potential mismatch issue).

issues.label: Consecutive sentencing findings
issues.why: For any consecutive non-spec terms, the court must make and journalize R.C. 2929.14(C)(4) findings.

issues.label: Consecutive reasons at hearing
issues.why: The court must state the consecutive findings at the sentencing hearing, not merely in the entry.

issues.label: Consecutive for failure-to-comply
issues.why: The court must determine whether the failure-to-comply term was ordered consecutive lawfully and with required findings.

issues.label: Consecutive for vehicular homicide
issues.why: The court must determine whether making aggravated vehicular homicide consecutive was supported by required findings.

issues.label: Concurrent across cases legality
issues.why: The court must confirm the trial court had authority to order concurrent service between the two case sentences and did so correctly.

issues.label: Aggregate sentence computation
issues.why: The court must verify the arithmetic and structure (spec time + base terms + concurrency) matches the stated totals.

issues.label: Postrelease control advisements
issues.why: The court must properly impose and notify Hampton of PRC for each felony and include it correctly in the entry.

issues.label: Mandatory PRC accuracy
issues.why: The court must ensure PRC is mandatory/discretionary as dictated by each offense level and properly stated.

issues.label: Jail-time credit determination
issues.why: The court must address whether jail-time credit was calculated and applied correctly across consolidated/concurrent cases.

issues.label: Credit allocation across cases
issues.why: The court must ensure credit is not unlawfully duplicated or withheld when sentences run concurrently in separate cases.

issues.label: Court costs and indigency
issues.why: The court must impose costs consistent with law and consider any waiver issues if properly raised.

issues.label: Fines and restitution authority
issues.why: If imposed, fines/restitution must be authorized, supported by evidence, and follow statutory procedures.

issues.label: Forfeiture specification compliance
issues.why: The court must ensure forfeiture findings, nexus, and procedures (including notice and entry terms) comply with Ohio forfeiture law.

issues.label: Disposition of weapon forfeiture
issues.why: The court must address lawful seizure/forfeiture of the 3-D-printed firearm/dangerous ordnance and any required orders.

issues.label: Victim rights allocution
issues.why: The court must ensure victims were afforded rights to be heard and that victim-impact input was properly considered.

issues.label: Defendant allocution
issues.why: The court must ensure Hampton was afforded allocution under Crim.R. 32(A) before sentence was imposed.

issues.label: Consideration of PSI
issues.why: The court must confirm it considered the PSI and that any disputed facts were handled appropriately.

issues.label: R.C. 2929.11 purposes
issues.why: The court must consider felony-sentencing purposes and principles and ensure the sentence is consistent with them.

issues.label: R.C. 2929.12 factors
issues.why: The court must consider seriousness and recidivism factors and avoid reliance on improper factors.

issues.label: Sentencing entry completeness
issues.why: The judgment entries must include conviction, sentence, PRC, and consecutive findings where required to be valid.

issues.label: Contrary-to-law standard
issues.why: The reviewing court must apply R.C. 2953.08(G)(2) to decide whether the sentence is contrary to law or unsupported by the record.

issues.label: Eighth Amendment proportionality
issues.why: The court must address whether the sentence is grossly disproportionate to the offenses under federal constitutional standards.

issues.label: Ohio cruel-punishment clause
issues.why: The court must analyze proportionality under Article I, Section 9 of the Ohio Constitution if separately argued.

issues.label: Due process in sentencing
issues.why: The court must ensure sentencing was not based on materially false information and complied with procedural due process.

issues.label: Equal protection considerations
issues.why: If raised, the court must determine whether Hampton was treated differently without a rational basis in sentencing.

issues.label: Art I Sec 16 due course
issues.why: The court must consider any Ohio due-course-of-law claim related to sentencing procedure or legality.

issues.label: Fifth Amendment self-incrimination
issues.why: The court must consider whether sentencing penalized Hampton for silence or compelled statements in violation of the Fifth Amendment.

issues.label: Use of dismissed conduct
issues.why: The court must consider whether the court relied on dismissed/uncharged conduct and whether such reliance was permissible and supported.

issues.label: Reliance on merger-barred conduct
issues.why: If offenses should have merged, the court must ensure the sentence did not improperly punish the same conduct twice.

issues.label: Double jeopardy implications
issues.why: Merger/dismissal/consolidation issues may implicate constitutional double jeopardy protections.

issues.label: Competency at sentencing
issues.why: The court must ensure Hampton was competent during plea and sentencing proceedings if any indicator existed.

issues.label: Counsel effectiveness at sentencing
issues.why: If implicated, the court must consider whether counsel’s performance affected sentencing legality or required findings.

issues.label: Interpretation of plea agreement
issues.why: The court must determine whether the sentence complied with any agreed recommendations or caps and whether any breach occurred.

issues.label: Sentencing package doctrine limits
issues.why: The court must avoid altering lawful components based on errors elsewhere without proper authority on remand.

issues.label: Record sufficiency for review
issues.why: The court must ensure the transcript/entries allow meaningful review of statutory findings and constitutional claims.
